HTTP-Anfragen laufen über den Vite-Proxy: HTTP requests go through the Vite proxy (dev) or straight to the Spring Boot backend, pass Spring Security with the `ApiKeyAuthFilter` and the `RateLimitFilter`, and end up in the REST controllers. Services send live messages via STOMP.
Reihenfolge: Spring Security mit `ApiKey: Order: Spring Security with `ApiKeyAuthFilter` → `RateLimitFilter` → controller. Without a valid key, Spring Security rejects protected paths with 403 before any business logic runs; the rate limit only counts `/api/**`.

Controller sind schlank; Services kapsel: Controllers are thin; services encapsulate logic and transactions, repositories talk to SQLite over a single connection (HikariCP `maximum-pool-size: 1`). Open Session in View is off: lazy loading belongs in the service, the controller maps to DTOs with MapStruct.
